gen-dafont-nordic-gf-liter: Nordic spaces its letters far apart, like brush dabs on paper, with a cramped, folded opening in each one. And Liter, a sans with no stroke contrast and wide mouths on its round forms, is the open, upright partner.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-mada: Ancient, weighty, stamped. Nordic keeps one constant pen line throughout, and Mada's sans-serif curves refuse to close above a towering midzone, so the two meet on the page as old and new.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-martel-sans: Martel Sans reads as a sans with generous openings in every curve and a high mean line across each word. But Nordic is the one to lean on for powerful, ancient, cramped shapes, while Martel Sans handles the open, modern running text.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-matangi: Powerful and ancient, Nordic closes its letters tight against the rounded, left-open forms of a hefty lowercase in Matangi. Strokes like pressed twine make Matangi the softer voice.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-maven-pro: Nordic's brush-dab spacing, set far apart across the paper, is the first thing you notice about it. Maven Pro takes over where that gets tight, offering a welcoming gap in the c and a high-waisted lowercase, while Nordic keeps the heavy, ancient voice.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-michroma: Nordic ends each terminal at the same width it began, with a cramped opening like a pressed leaf fold. Michroma gives every letter a wide berth and leaves daylight in its curves, so a long passage would feel spacious and unhurried.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-miriam-libre: Powerful and ancient, Nordic stands tight and closed up top. Miriam Libre follows in plain sans, with a drawn-wire weight and an s that opens generously, so a longer passage would feel approachable and sturdy.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-mochiy-pop-one: Mochiy Pop One hangs its very large lowercase eyes on a long line, like clothespins, under Nordic's powerful, closed-up display letters. Its single stroke width gives the pair its strongest quality.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-mochiy-pop-p-one: Nordic's letters sit far apart like brush dabs on paper, each one with a cramped, folded opening and a monoweight stroke. Mochiy Pop P One counters with a sizable lowercase and wide gaps between letters.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-montserrat-underlin: Montserrat Underline reads open, its counters breathing like a hollow reed and its lowercase looking oversized beside the capitals. Nordic does powerful, ancient and closed best, while the sans-serif body does open, even-walled bowls best.
